messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] apac-primary GPU serving pool queue depth > 90% (queue=1,860). Autoscaler reported repeated failures. Paging @Kendra (oncall) @Marco (eng-runtime) @Infra-Lead. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood/1858004321

Kendra (oncall): joining. seeing a lot of 5xx/timeout traces on the dashboard. queue growth started ~11:02 UTC.

Marco (eng-runtime): looking at autoscaler logs now. `scale_attempt_failed: quota_exceeded` x4 in last 7m. also a couple of OOMs on the leader pod right before spike.

SRE-Bot: autoscaler events (recent):
- 11:05:34 scale_attempt id=sa-717 fail=quota_exceeded region=apac-east1
- 11:07:50 scale_attempt id=sa-718 fail=rate_limit region=apac-east1
- 11:09:12 scale_attempt id=sa-719 fail=quota_exceeded region=apac-east1

Alex: noticed routing spillover kicking in to eu-west1 because apac-primary returning 429/503. but eu-west1 is near its own threshold (70%); spillover is just amplifying load.

Jamie - CS: getting pings from Streamly (enterprise). they see burst 504s for streaming completions. they want ETA.

Priya: streaming endpoints are most sensitive. can we temporarily throttle long-running streaming sessions or deprioritize dev/org sandbox traffic?

Kendra (oncall): yes. first quick mitigations:
1) flip routing policy for apac-primary to prefer local only (stop spillover)
2) apply emergency throttle to non-critical routes (dev/sandbox)
3) attempt manual scale of dedicated gpu pool if infra-claim permits

Marco (eng-runtime): do we have permission for manual scale? Infra-Lead: can you approve a hot scale of reserved pool (apac-hot) + add quota request?

Infra-Lead: I approve temporary manual scale up of apac-hot by +8 GPUs. quota request still pending; manual nodes will be from reserved spare capacity. doing now.

DevEx: runbook note — see runbook section 'cross-region spillover' for traffic steering commands.

Marco (eng-runtime): executing routing flip. command:
```
# patch routing policy to disable spillover
curl -X POST https://routing.api/redwood/v1/policies/apac-primary/actions -d '{"spillover_allowed":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

SRE-Bot: routing policy update success 11:18:02. spillover disabled.

Kendra (oncall): applying throttle to sandbox/org=dev routes: 50% token rate limit.

Marco (eng-runtime): manual scale request submitted to infra: `scale_pool apac-hot --gpus 8 --reason "incident 1858004321 emergency"`. infra confirmed nodes provisioning 11:20:08.

SRE-Bot: pool apac-hot status: provisioning -> ready (11:29:14).

Alex: after enabling new nodes we're seeing queue drain but still high tail latency on streaming. some requests still routed to apac-fallback zone (apac-fallback1) which is disabled for inference caches. we should flip fallback to use same serving config.

Marco (eng-runtime): noticed autoscaler deadlock: it stopped scaling because leader pod couldn't update cluster state due to transient DB timeout. root cause: RPS spike caused DB connection pool exhaustion; autoscaler retries then hit quota. Filed a ticket to tighten DB timeouts.

Priya: CS says Streamly spike subsided after 11:34 but they still saw retries. they want post-incident summary.

Jamie - CS: we told them temporary mitigation and asked them to reroute non-prod traffic. they're happy with the manual scale for now.

Kendra (oncall): after mitigations queue dropped to 420 by 11:35 and to 90 by 11:45. tail latencies still slightly elevated.

Marco (eng-runtime): follow-up actions:
- revert spillover disable after cluster fully healthy (controlled canary)
- add autoscaler fallback to use apac-hot when apac-primary leader unhealthy
- increase DB connection pool for autoscaler and add circuit breaker
- audit routing policy to avoid cascading spillover when neighbouring region >60%

Infra-Lead: recommend creating CR for emergency quota visibility and autoscaler leader health checks.

DevEx: I'll update the runbook with the exact CLI snippets and add a pre-flight checklist to verify fallback region headroom before enabling spillover.

Kendra (oncall): handing off to Priya for the post-incident follow up and overnight watch. Priya, you're the owner for next 12h. I'll write the initial incident ticket and summary.

Priya: taking handoff. will coordinate postmortem and customer comms. adding reminders:
- invite infra and runtime to postmortem
- collect autoscaler + DB logs from 11:00-11:40 UTC
- get Streamly timeline and ask for any request ids

Jamie - CS: sending Streamly a short note now, will include timeline and mitigations.

Kendra (oncall): incident severity set to Sev2. creating INC-2026-134 and attaching logs.

SRE-Bot: incident INC-2026-134 created and assigned to Priya.

Marco (eng-runtime): final note — primary root: autoscaler leader health + quota exhaustion + permissive spillover rules. will propose config changes in next-day RFC.

Priya: thanks team. I'll post the incident summary in #incidents-summary after the investigation. leaving this thread open for any late artifacts.
